attempts.reason_tested: already published: canine severity data on NETs, cfDNA, histones, calprotectin or released MPO/elastase
attempts.method: Grep of /core/articles/*.md and /core/data/markdown/CB*.md for extracellular trap, NETosis, cell-free DNA, cfDNA, nucleosome, calprotectin, S100A8/A9/A12, citrullinated, histone, myeloperoxidase, neutrophil elastase, lactoferrin. PubMed: '(dog OR dogs OR canine) AND (babesia OR babesiosis) AND (neutrophil extracellular traps OR NETosis OR cell-free DNA OR nucleosomes OR histones OR citrullinated)'; '(dog OR dogs OR canine) AND (babesia OR babesiosis) AND (calprotectin OR S100A12 OR S100A8 OR S100A9 OR elastase OR myeloperoxidase OR lactoferrin)'; '(Babesia rossi OR Babesia canis OR Babesia gibsoni OR Babesia vogeli) AND neutrophil'.
attempts.result: No CB article measures NETs, cfDNA, nucleosomes, circulating histones, calprotectin, S100A12 or plasma MPO/elastase in dogs with babesiosis. NET mentions in CB028, CB098, CB141, CB145 are discussion only; the 2023 review CB107 states that NETosis has not been studied in canine babesiosis. PubMed returned 4 and 8 records; none is a measurement (the cfDNA hit 10.1016/j.ygeno.2018.05.020 sequenced cfDNA to detect Babesia DNA, not host NETs; 10.1016/j.cimid.2017.06.001 and 10.1186/s12917-017-1020-9 only mention elastase or oxidants). The 30 Babesia-neutrophil records include CB050 (MPXI) and none on NETs. Nearest published canine findings: CB112 (10.1038/s41598-023-37312-9) reported serum lactotransferrin, a secondary-granule protein, across control, uncomplicated and complicated groups; CB050 (10.3389/fvets.2020.00072) cellular MPXI higher in non-survivors than controls; CB040 band neutrophils raise odds of death. The gap for NETs and released granule proteins stands; the 'degranulation' part is partly anticipated by CB112 lactoferrin.

attempts.reason_tested: restatement of published band-neutrophil and MPXI findings (more neutrophils, left shift)
attempts.method: Read /core/articles/CB050_*.md, CB040_*.md; DS07 label definition in /experiments/shared/tidy/DS07.outcomes.json; SV-08 construct check in /experiments/SV-08/report.md; S100A8 vs LTF correlation in DS07 (script /experiments/SV-META/refutation/scripts/K04_neutrophil_checks.py).
attempts.result: As a hypothesis, NET release and extracellular granule proteins are a mechanism distinct from neutrophil number or cellular MPO content (released MPO would be expected to move opposite to MPXI). But every piece of supporting canine data is confounded with neutrophil number and left shift: the DS07 'complicated' label includes band neutrophils > 1.5 x10^9/L, and DS07 has no leukocyte or neutrophil counts to adjust for; the SV-08 neutrophil-granule transcript score tracks band neutrophils (median per-dog rho +0.80) and the report itself says the rise may be a left shift, not a change per cell; in DS07, S100A8 and lactoferrin correlate (rho 0.48, n 25, p 0.015) and S100A8 adjusted for lactoferrin falls to rho 0.24 (-0.22 to 0.69). Existing data cannot separate 'NETs/degranulation' from 'more immature neutrophils'.

attempts.reason_tested: does not survive correction for the number of tests
attempts.result: S100A8 complicated minus uncomplicated +0.43 log2 (-0.10 to +0.93), p 0.12, q 0.29; histone H4 untestable (2 plexes, 4 vs 2 dogs); only the positive control lactoferrin is nominal (p 0.027, q 0.13). Nothing in the K04 family passes correction. S100A8 also shows no infected-vs-control difference (delta +0.007, p 0.98), which is odd for a neutrophil-activation alarmin in a strongly inflammatory disease.

attempts.reason_tested: confounder: haemolysis / red-cell burden (HBB) and general acute-phase response
attempts.method: K04_neutrophil_checks.py: plex-median-centred DS07 values, Spearman partial correlation of S100A8 or LTF with complicated (infected dogs), covariates HBB (P60524), CRP (T2KEN6), SAA (A0A5F4D168); bootstrap by dog, 2000 resamples, seed 20261112.
attempts.result: S100A8: unadjusted rho 0.37 (-0.10 to 0.74), n 26 (10 complicated); +CRP 0.35; +SAA 0.38; +HBB 0.25 (-0.21 to 0.66); +HBB+CRP 0.24 (-0.25 to 0.69). Lactoferrin: unadjusted 0.40 (0.03 to 0.72), n 31; +HBB 0.18 (-0.20 to 0.57); +HBB+CRP 0.19. The acute-phase response does not explain the signal, but adjusting for serum haemoglobin removes about a third (S100A8) to a half (LTF) of it. HBB is partly a severity feature itself (haematocrit < 0.15 is in the label), so this may be over-adjustment, but the signal cannot be separated from haemolysis in these data.

attempts.reason_tested: severity gradient in the experimental Beagles (SV-08)
attempts.result: Neutrophil-granule score rose in 5 of 5 dogs (sign test p 0.0625), including both mild low-dose dogs. High-dose dogs (+0.17, +0.28, +0.19) all exceed low-dose dogs (+0.10, +0.13) (exact rank test p 0.2 two-sided), but dose is aliased with dog and the dog that died (+0.19) is not the highest. MPO and ELANE (the promyelocyte genes central to the human signature) are not in the filtered DS06 matrix. No severity gradient is shown; this is a response to infection.

attempts.reason_tested: assay and sample artefact (haemolysis, icterus, serum versus plasma)
attempts.result: Canine assays exist: cfDNA by benchtop fluorometry is linear and repeatable (10.1111/vec.12592) and cfDNA per neutrophil was higher in septic non-survivors (10.1111/vec.12773); the commercial nucleosome ELISA showed large positive interference from haemolysis and icterus in canine IMHA (10.1016/j.vetimm.2015.10.014), a direct problem in haemolytic, icteric B. rossi; canine calprotectin and S100A12 radioimmunoassays are analytically validated (10.2460/ajvr.69.7.845; 10.1016/j.vetimm.2011.09.011); the canine elastase ELISA has spiking recovery of 27 to 114 percent (10.2460/ajvr.68.6.584). DS07 is archived serum: neutrophil granule proteins can be released ex vivo during clotting (inferred, not tested here), so a prospective study would need plasma. The lead is testable but not with the nucleosome ELISA without interference controls.

Evidence comes from SRC-C (DS07) and SRC-B (DS06/SV-08) only, two independent sources; SV-06a is a literature ranking, not data. No double counting, but no natural-infection outcome cohort (SRC-A) contributes, and DS07 may share numbering with DS04.

verdict_reason: The gap is real: no study has measured NETs, cfDNA, nucleosomes, circulating histones, calprotectin or released MPO/elastase against severity or outcome in canine babesiosis, and CB107 states NETosis is unstudied. The canine support is weak and confounded: no signal passes correction (S100A8 q 0.29, H4 untestable), half the lactoferrin and a third of the S100A8 effect go with serum haemoglobin, the DS07 label contains band neutrophils, and SV-08 shows a response to infection with no severity gradient that tracks band counts. It remains a literature-driven gap lead, not a data-supported finding, and the human evidence itself is mixed.

human_counterpart.claim: Plasma neutrophil elastase, MPO and proteinase 3 (not lactoferrin or lipocalin) higher in retinopathy-positive paediatric cerebral malaria; neutrophil transcripts most upregulated; but no NETs found in brain autopsy microvasculature (HU005)
In 341 ICU patients an ex vivo NET-forming assay predicted DIC and death independently of APACHE II, whereas cfDNA, MPO and MPO-DNA complexes did not (HU008)
Circulating extracellular histones, about equally host and parasite origin, are raised in paediatric cerebral malaria and associated with brain swelling (HU021)
Whole-blood neutrophil degranulation genes (ELANE, MPO, PRTN3, CEACAM8, DEFA4) higher in 30-day sepsis non-survivors after adjustment for neutrophil count, replicated in a second cohort (HU006)

Neutrophil granule gene expression associated with all severe malaria phenotypes in Gambian children, but up to 99 percent of host differential expression was driven by parasite load (Lee et al. 2018)

canine_parallel_already_made: partly: NETs, cfDNA, histones, calprotectin and released MPO/elastase have not been measured in canine babesiosis (only speculated in CB107, CB098, CB028, CB141, CB145); related neutrophil findings are published: lactoferrin across severity groups (CB112), cellular MPXI higher in non-survivors than controls (CB050), band neutrophils with death (CB040)
